scientific_hypothesis: Anchoring the first 4 AR-matching layers to quarter-wavelength thickness estimates at the telecom band center (1547.5 nm) will reduce early-round search entropy and enable the optimizer to more efficiently discover high-transmittance solutions in the 1530-1565 nm band while maintaining visible reflectance through the remaining 16 Bragg layers.
expected_advantages: Reduced search space dimensionality for AR section accelerates convergence
Quarter-wave initialization provides physically meaningful starting point
Maintains full optimization freedom for Bragg section to tune visible rejection
known_risks: Quarter-wave anchoring may constrain AR section from discovering superior non-quarter-wave solutions
Fixed 20-layer count may not be optimal for this dual-band requirement
expected_observations: best_target_score should exceed the prior iteration's 0.6013 if the bounded search successfully redirects density to superior local minima.
tightest_margin should deviate from the prior 0.4296 value consistent with the hypothesis that thickness bounding alters the robustness landscape.
max(thicknesses_nm) across all valid candidates must not exceed 280nm.
valid_candidates should remain > 0 indicating the 280nm bound is not infeasible for this topology.
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improvement relative to historical best is < 1e-3 for 2 consecutive rounds, judge search as stagnated -> stop and retain current best.
If valid_candidates = 0, judge constraint set infeasible -> should relax thickness bound to 300nm, not re-run the same route.
If max(thicknesses_nm) exceeds 280nm in any valid candidate, judge bound enforcement failed -> stop and verify optimizer constraint implementation.
